title: Outcomes After Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Combination With Bezlotoxumab for Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection.
population: adults with inflammatory bowel disease and recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection
cure_fmt: 26/30 (87%) no CDI recurrence in bezlotoxumab arm
cure_comparator: 30/31 (97%) no CDI recurrence in placebo arm
key_finding: FMT combined with bezlotoxumab was not superior to FMT plus placebo for preventing CDI recurrence in IBD patients (13% vs 3% recurrence rate, P = 0.15).

title: Faecal microbiota transplantation for first or second Clostridioides difficile infection (EarlyFMT): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
population: adults aged ≥18 years with first or second Clostridioides difficile infection
primary_outcome: resolution of C. difficile-associated diarrhoea (CDAD) 8 weeks after treatment
serious_adverse_events: 3 SAEs possibly related to study treatment (1 in FMT group, 2 in placebo group); no deaths or colectomies
key_finding: FMT after vancomycin for first or second CDI was highly effective, achieving CDAD resolution in 90% vs 33% with placebo at 8 weeks; trial stopped early for ethical reasons.

title: Randomised clinical trial: a 12-strain bacterial mixture versus faecal microbiota transplantation versus vancomycin for recurrent Clostridioides difficile infections.
population: adults with laboratory-confirmed recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection
key_finding: FMT by enema achieved clinical cure in 76% of recurrent CDI patients, superior to vancomycin (45%) and 12-strain rectal bacteriotherapy (52%).

title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation Is Superior to Fidaxomicin for Treatment of Recurrent Clostridium difficile Infection.
population: consecutive adults with recurrent Clostridium difficile infection
primary_outcome: combined clinical resolution and negative PCR test for C. difficile toxin 8 weeks after treatment
key_finding: FMT after vancomycin was superior to fidaxomicin and vancomycin monotherapy for combined clinical and microbiological resolution of recurrent CDI (71% vs 33% vs 19%).

title: Randomised clinical trial: faecal microbiota transplantation by colonoscopy plus vancomycin for the treatment of severe refractory Clostridium difficile infection-single versus multiple infusions.
population: adults with severe Clostridium difficile infection refractory to antibiotics
primary_outcome: cure of severe refractory Clostridium difficile infection
serious_adverse_events: No serious adverse events in either group
key_finding: Multiple FMT infusions guided by pseudomembrane resolution were significantly more effective than a single FMT plus vancomycin (100% vs 75% cure rate, P = 0.01) for severe refractory CDI.

title: Effect of Oral Capsule- vs Colonoscopy-Delivered Fecal Microbiota Transplantation on Recurrent Clostridium difficile Infection: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: adults with recurrent Clostridium difficile infection
primary_outcome: proportion of patients without RCDI 12 weeks after FMT
serious_adverse_events: 1 death in each group unrelated to FMT; minor AEs 5.4% capsule vs 12.5% colonoscopy
key_finding: FMT via oral capsules was noninferior to colonoscopy delivery for preventing recurrent CDI at 12 weeks (96.2% in both groups per-protocol).

title: Randomised clinical trial: faecal microbiota transplantation for recurrent Clostridum difficile infection - fresh, or frozen, or lyophilised microbiota from a small pool of healthy donors delivered by colonoscopy.
population: adults with ≥3 bouts of recurrent Clostridium difficile infection
key_finding: Overall CDI resolution was 87% with colonoscopy-delivered FMT; fresh product achieved 100% cure, superior to lyophilized (78%, P = 0.022 vs fresh), with frozen intermediate (83%).

title: Oral Vancomycin Followed by Fecal Transplantation Versus Tapering Oral Vancomycin Treatment for Recurrent Clostridium difficile Infection: An Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: adults with acute recurrence of Clostridium difficile infection
serious_adverse_events: Adverse events similar and uncommon in both groups
key_finding: A single FMT by enema was not significantly better than vancomycin taper for recurrent CDI (43.8% vs 58.3% symptom resolution); trial stopped at interim analysis due to futility.

title: Effect of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation on Recurrence in Multiply Recurrent Clostridium difficile Infection: A Randomized Trial.
population: adults with ≥3 recurrences of Clostridium difficile infection
primary_outcome: resolution of diarrhea without further anti-CDI therapy during 8-week follow-up
key_finding: Donor FMT via colonoscopy was more efficacious than autologous FMT for preventing CDI recurrence (90.9% vs 62.5%, P = 0.042).

title: Frozen vs Fresh Fecal Microbiota Transplantation and Clinical Resolution of Diarrhea in Patients With Recurrent Clostridium difficile Infection: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: adults with recurrent or refractory Clostridium difficile infection
primary_outcome: clinical resolution of diarrhea without relapse at 13 weeks
serious_adverse_events: No differences in adverse or serious adverse events between groups
key_finding: Frozen FMT was noninferior to fresh FMT via enema for clinical resolution of recurrent/refractory CDI (83.5% vs 85.1% per-protocol).

title: Randomised clinical trial: faecal microbiota transplantation by colonoscopy vs. vancomycin for the treatment of recurrent Clostridium difficile infection.
population: adults with recurrent Clostridium difficile infection
primary_outcome: resolution of C. difficile-associated diarrhoea 10 weeks after end of treatments
serious_adverse_events: No significant adverse events in either group
key_finding: FMT via colonoscopy achieved significantly higher resolution of recurrent CDI than vancomycin (90% vs 26%, P < 0.0001); trial stopped early at interim analysis.

title: Fecal microbiota transplant for relapsing Clostridium difficile infection using a frozen inoculum from unrelated donors: a randomized, open-label, controlled pilot study.
population: adults with relapsing/refractory Clostridium difficile infection
primary_outcome: clinical resolution of diarrhea without relapse after 8 weeks
serious_adverse_events: No serious or unexpected adverse events
key_finding: FMT using frozen inoculum from unrelated donors was effective for relapsing CDI (70% after single treatment, 90% overall after retreatment), with no significant difference between colonoscopic and NGT delivery.

title: Safety and preliminary efficacy of orally administered lyophilized fecal microbiota product compared with frozen product given by enema for recurrent Clostridium difficile infection: A randomized clinical trial.
population: adults with ≥3 episodes of recurrent Clostridium difficile infection
cure_fmt: 26/31 (84%) lyophilized capsule group (no CDI recurrence at 60 days)
serious_adverse_events: Adverse experiences equally frequent in both groups; not related to route of delivery
key_finding: Oral lyophilized FMT and frozen FMT by enema showed comparable safety and preliminary efficacy for recurrent CDI (84% vs 88% prevention of recurrence at 60 days, P = 0.76).
